test_title: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-1 (Held On: 14 Nov, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Unnat Gram Abhiyan, launched in 2024 is specifically targeted at ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Tribal communities in aspirational areas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Unnat Gram Abhiyan** was launched in **2024** by the Government of India to promote the holistic development of **tribal communities** in designated **aspirational areas**.
 
• The initiative aims to address the socio-economic disparities faced by tribal communities by focusing on **healthcare, education, skill development, and infrastructure development**.
 
• The scheme prioritizes areas identified under the **‘Aspirational Districts Programme’**, targeting regions with significant tribal populations and low Human Development Index (HDI).
 
• It seeks to promote sustainable livelihoods and economic empowerment for tribal people through initiatives like **agriculture support, forest-based economy enhancement, and micro-enterprise development**.
 
• The scheme is aligned with the goals of **inclusivity, equity, and social justice**, ensuring that tribal communities are not left behind in India's development journey.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Aspirational Districts Programme (ADP):**

 
 
• Launched in **2018**, ADP aims to transform 112 backward districts in India by improving key indicators in **health, nutrition, education, agriculture, financial inclusion, and skill development**.
 
• The programme emphasizes a **data-driven approach** and promotes competition among districts to achieve progress.
 
• Tribal-dominated areas form a major part of these districts, making them a focus for inclusive development initiatives like Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Unnat Gram Abhiyan.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of Tribal Development Schemes:**
 
 
• Programs like **Van Dhan Yojana** support tribal entrepreneurs through **value addition of Minor Forest Produce (MFP)** and marketing support.
 
• **Educational initiatives** such as Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) provide quality education to tribal children in remote areas.
 
• Healthcare-focused schemes aim at reducing maternal and infant mortality rates among tribal populations through institutional deliveries and immunization drives.
 
 
 
• **Socio-economic Challenges Faced by Tribal Communities:**
 
 
• Tribal communities often face issues like **poverty, illiteracy, malnutrition, and lack of healthcare facilities**.
 
• They are heavily dependent on natural resources and face challenges due to **deforestation, climate change, and displacement**.
 
 
 
• **Other Government Initiatives for Tribal Welfare:**
 
 
• The **Integrated Tribal Development Project (ITDP)** focuses on improving living standards in tribal areas.
 
• The **Tribal Sub-Plan (TSP)** allocates funds for the welfare of Scheduled Tribes in various sectors.
 
• **Skill development programs** aim to provide employment opportunities to tribal youth in various trades and industries.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Tribal population in India:** According to the **2011 Census**, tribal communities constitute approximately **8.6%** of India's total population, with significant concentration in states like **Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, and Rajasthan**.
 
• **Article 46 of the Indian Constitution:** It directs the State to promote the educational and economic interests of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and other weaker sections.
 
• **Forest Rights Act, 2006:** Provides recognition and vesting of forest rights to forest-dwelling communities, ensuring their livelihood and cultural preservation.
